# Test data

Sample logs used by the test suite.

Every file here needs a row in the table below. A log without recorded
provenance gets removed.

| File | Source | Generated by | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `good.ulg` | Synthetic. Not a recording of any real flight. | `crates/vane-core/tests/fixtures.rs`, written to the published ULog specification | MIT OR Apache-2.0, same as this repository |
| `crash.ulg` | Synthetic. Not a recording of any real flight. | `crates/vane-core/tests/fixtures.rs`, written to the published ULog specification | MIT OR Apache-2.0, same as this repository |
| `truncated.ulg` | Synthetic. `good.ulg` cut mid-parameter-message. | `crates/vane-core/tests/fixtures.rs`, written to the published ULog specification | MIT OR Apache-2.0, same as this repository |

These three carry no location history and no telemetry, because nothing ever
flew to produce them. They exercise the parser against the format as
specified, which is not the same as the format as firmware actually writes
it. A SITL corpus is still worth having before trusting the parser on
someone's real crash.

## Regenerating

```sh
VANE_REGENERATE_FIXTURES=1 cargo test -p vane-core --test fixtures
```

Without that variable the same test compares the committed bytes against what
the generator would produce, so a fixture edited by hand fails the suite.

## Generating logs from SITL

Prefer SITL over real flights, so the corpus is reproducible and carries no
location history.

```sh
# PX4
make px4_sitl gazebo-classic     # logs land in build/px4_sitl_default/rootfs/log/

# ArduPilot
sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map
```

Truncated fixtures are made by copying a good log and cutting it short:

```sh
head -c 40000 good.ulg > truncated.ulg
```
